subject: ventures/feie-physical-presence-calculator
professional: an enrolled agent / CPA who prepares Form 2555 for US expats (checks first: full 24-hour days, the 12-month period rule incl. leap years, choosing the period with the greatest exclusion, the year's exclusion limit, and proration by qualifying days with a foreign tax home)

evidence.correctness: Fetched the IRS sources (irs.gov 'Foreign Earned Income Exclusion - Physical Presence Test' page, reviewed 14-Mar-2026; Instructions for Form 2555 (2026); Pub 54 (12/2025)) and wrote an independent Python brute force (scratchpad feie/indep.py: every 12-month period 'begins any day, ends the day before the same calendar day 12 months later', counts full foreign days, picks the period with the greatest overlap of the tax year, prorates limit x days / days-in-year). Compared with `node -e analyze(...)`: sample best 347 days from 2025-02-03, earliest 2025-09-04, 365 qualifying days, excluded 95,000 = same; IRS New Zealand example (abroad 2024-01-01..2025-08-31 less 28 days each February): 2024 window Jan 1-Dec 31 2024, 366 days, 126,500 = IRS's stated 2024 period; 2025 best 338 days, earliest 2024-12-23 match; arrival 2026-08-14 with the 2026 limit 132,900 (confirmed in i2555 2026 'What's New'): 175 qualifying days, 63,719.18 = same. Every recomputed output matched my model. Gaps: a tax year outside 2023-2026 silently uses the 2025 limit (2022 -> 130,000, IRS figure 112,000; 2027 -> 130,000), and qualifying days extend past the last foreign day (NZ 2025: 250 days/89,041.10 vs the IRS example's chosen period giving 243 days/86,547.95), valid only if the tax home stayed abroad.
evidence.completeness: Ran `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the subject: 17/17 pass (engine.test.mjs, page.test.mjs). Checked each README/page feature through analyze()/summarize(): best 12-month window, 330 count, slack and days elsewhere (maxOutside 35 on sample), first date reaching 330, prorated exclusion and income cap, per-year foreign-day table, editable limit, 'present' stays, comment lines, error lines, copy summary text. Guide page and its worked numbers match the engine (page.test). served-copy.mjs: no placeholder or retired origin. No stubs or TODOs. All claimed features work.
evidence.verification: 17 tests pass and pin the 330/329 boundary, any-day window start, leap-year 366, the sample and the guide's numbers. quality_mutate.py: 3 of 6 core mutants survive: prorating by 365 instead of days-in-year (engine.mjs:107), excluded = min(income, limit) dropping proration entirely (engine.mjs:108), and the earliest-date window shifted to a 366-day span (engine.mjs:86, non-equivalent: on '2024-01-01 to 2024-01-01 / 2024-02-08 to 2025-01-01' the mutant reports 2025-01-01 as the qualifying date while the best window holds 329). Caught: 366-day best window (:80), >= to > (:90), qualifying-window threshold (:102). The prorated test asserts qDaysInYear and prorated but income 100,000 is below the prorated cap, so 'excluded' is never checked against proration.
evidence.craft: Read engine.mjs (141 lines), index.html script, usage.mjs, both test files. Pure functions, strict date parsing that rejects 2025-02-29, a prefix-sum day counter, HTML escaped on output, storage guarded. Defects: silent fallback `LIMITS[taxYear] ?? LIMITS[2025]` (engine.mjs:68) for any year the input accepts (2000-2100); engine's default asOf is the UTC date (the page overrides with local); a 'what-if' comment over a plain shortfall (engine.mjs:114); the window loop is duplicated (lines 79 and 100) but cheap.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer (no warranty, not tax advice, verify, not affiliated) on index.html:107 and the guide, asserted by page.test. 'Nothing is uploaded' backed: page.test asserts no fetch/XMLHttpRequest/sendBeacon/remote script; DNT and GPC honoured (usage.mjs usageBlocked). Limit table 2023 120,000 / 2024 126,500 / 2025 130,000 / 2026 132,900 matches Rev. Procs and i2555 (2026). Sample numbers on page FAQ, guide and llms.txt match the engine. Weak: README says the prorated limit uses 'the days of the tax year that fall in some qualifying window' but the code takes the single window with the largest overlap (engine.mjs:99-106), which matches Form 2555 line 16 but not the README; README says the limit table is editable, true, but not that years outside it fall back silently.
evidence.fitness: Walked the expat's job: paste stays, see whether a 12-month window clears 330, how many spare days a US trip may use, when 330 is first reached, and the prorated exclusion for a tax year. Works in seconds; output gives a preparer the Form 2555 line 16 dates and the qualifying-day count. A move or return year still needs the preparer to trim qualifying days to the foreign-tax-home period, and travel days must be removed by hand.
evidence.domain: Compared with the IRS physical presence page, i2555 (2026) and Pub 54: the any-day 12-month period (incl. Feb 29 start), full-day counting, 'choose the 12-month period that gives you the greatest exclusion', proration by days in the year and the income cap are right. Departures a preparer hits early: (1) qualifying days are taken from the whole 12-month window, so they run up to 35 days before arrival and after departure (NZ example 250 vs 243; arrival 2026-08-14 gives 175 vs 140 days from the arrival date) with no result-level warning that i2555 defines the qualifying period as the time the tax home test is also met; (2) the input note says to remove 'the days you travelled', but the IRS says foreign-to-foreign moves under 24 hours lose no days, so users may undercount; (3) no war/civil-unrest waiver (annual Rev. Proc.); (4) income is capped at what is typed, without saying only pay for services abroad in the qualifying period counts.

defects.what: A tax year outside the 2023-2026 table silently uses the 2025 limit (2022 -> 130,000 vs IRS 112,000; 2027 -> 130,000) although the input accepts 2000-2100 and the field says 'blank = table'; an amended 2022 return would overstate the exclusion cap by 18,000.

Qualifying days for proration are the overlap of the whole 12-month window, so they run up to 35 days before arrival or after final departure (IRS NZ example: 250 days vs the 243 of the IRS's period; arrival 2026-08-14 gives 175 days) with no result-level warning that those days count only while the tax home is abroad (i2555 line 31 defines the qualifying period as when the tax home test is also met).

3 of 6 seeded core mutants survive: proration ignoring leap years, exclusion capped by the full limit instead of the prorated one, and the earliest-date window off by one day. The part-year test uses income below the prorated cap, so 'excluded' is never checked against proration, and no test has an earliest date that should be null.

Input note and page tell users to leave out every day they travelled; the IRS says moving between foreign countries in under 24 hours loses no full days, so users following it undercount (a false 'short' result).

README says the prorated limit counts days 'that fall in some qualifying window' (a union); the code uses the single window with the largest overlap, which matches Form 2555 line 16 but not the README.

Not modelled and not listed as such: the war/civil-unrest waiver of the 330-day minimum (annual Rev. Proc.), and that only pay for services performed abroad during the qualifying period is foreign earned income (the cap uses whatever income is typed).

verdict: A small, clean 330-day counter whose core date arithmetic is right. Against an independent brute force of the IRS 12-month rule and the IRS's own New Zealand example, the best window, day counts, earliest qualifying date, 2024 full-year period and the 2026 limit (132,900, confirmed in the 2026 Form 2555 instructions) all match; the disclaimer, no-upload and DNT claims hold. A Form 2555 preparer would push back in three places: a tax year outside 2023-2026 silently uses the 2025 limit (2022 shows 130,000, IRS 112,000); proration counts the whole 12-month window, so move and return years get up to 35 extra qualifying days (NZ 2025: 250 vs 243) without a tax-home warning; and the travel-day note over-removes foreign-to-foreign travel days. The 17 tests pass but miss 3 of 6 seeded core mutants, including dropping proration from the exclusion entirely. Does not meet the bar: verification 2 (correctness 3, claims 3, median 3). Finished (completeness 3). Fixable in one session: refuse or flag years without a table limit, warn when qualifying days fall outside the first-to-last foreign day, and add tests that pin 'excluded' to a prorated cap, leap-year proration and a null earliest date.
